# Matching models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

17 matching models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: two RGB images of one scene. Output: for every pixel of the first image its position in the second (x, y in pixels) and a certainty that the pixel is visible in both. Sparse matchers (LightGlue) return the keypoints of both images and the index pairs of the matched ones instead. To reconstruct camera poses from an image folder with these matchers, see [structure from motion](../sfm.md).

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 768x1024: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured; no kernels = the family has no kernels backend (reason under its table). Reserved memory is the allocator's cache: kernels (CUDA graphs, cuDNN workspaces) can reserve a few percent to some tens of percent more than portable at the same allocated peak.

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB (MLX)](../devices/apple-m1-pro-mlx-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

## FlexGlue

FlexGlue (ETH Zurich and partners, 2026): sparse matching of two photos of one scene: ALIKED keypoints, DINOv3 ConvNeXt features and a transformer that predicts where each keypoint lands in the other photo; keypoint index pairs. MIT; DINOv3 backbone weights under the DINOv3 licence.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aliked-flexglue` | synthetic (768x1024) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp32 | 348<br>129<br>129<br>96.1<br>328 (dense descriptor with eager ALIKED and matching) | 1801 / 1892<br>1775 / 1886<br>1814 / 2178<br>1762 / 1826<br>2225 / 2410 |

### Measured

Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. Both modes receive pairs resized to 768 x 1024. Map matched pixels to the calibrated evaluation coordinates and use the same RANSAC seed per pair. The same 300 pairs for all modes, so float32 and bfloat16 compare pair for pair. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

| `aliked-flexglue` | MegaDepth-1500, every 5th pair, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees | 50.8 / 68.2 / 80.4 | 51.5 / 69.1 / 81.0 | 51.9 / 69.3 / 81.1 | 51.5 / 69.1 / 81.0 |  |  |

Measured on portable: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 32e2e81e9, 2026-11-20; portable32: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 32e2e81e9 / 7eb2e0f4, 2026-11-18 to 2026-11-20; kernels: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 78a59767f, 2026-11-20; tensorrt: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 7eb2e0f4, 2026-11-18.

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.0001 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0052 and p99 <= 0.012 (absolute error of the output `keypoints1`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aliked-flexglue` | 0.00118 / 0.00319 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.10.0+cu130 | `image_normalize@592f5511307a:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; `pairs` are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
- One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the keypoint counts differ per image.
- No exportable module: the keypoint and match counts are data-dependent (`torch.compile` runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).
- Upstream's sparse mode only: no RoMa v2 refiner, no dense or sampled matches and no covisibility score.
- Two resizes per image as upstream: ALIKED sees a long side of `long_side` (aspect kept), the descriptor a `size` x `size` square whatever the aspect ratio.

</details>

Commercial use: yes.

### Limitations

- Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; `pairs` are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
- One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the keypoint counts differ per image.
- No exportable module: the keypoint counts are data-dependent (`torch.compile` runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).
- ALIKED-LightGlue has a fixed 768 x 1024 standalone FP32 TensorRT encoder measurement with TF32 disabled. Keypoint selection and LightGlue run in PyTorch. On 300 MegaDepth pairs, AUC@5 was 51.32 versus 49.75 portable FP32, with a worst paired pose error increase of 21.25 degrees.
- Computing DISK descriptors only at selected keypoints also changed pose outcomes. On a 100-pair MegaDepth check, both the PyTorch and TensorRT sparse projections changed a previously solved pair from 25.78 degrees to the 90-degree failure value, despite identical detected keypoints.

## DeDoDe v2

DeDoDe v2 (Chalmers, Linköping University; 3DV 2024): sparse keypoints from a detector network, descriptions from a separate one (VGG19, plus DINOv2 for -G), dual-softmax matches as keypoint index pairs (the form COLMAP takes). MIT; DINOv2 Apache-2.0.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |

- Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; `pairs` are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.

- Upright only: the released descriptors are not trained for in-plane rotations.

## LoFTR

LoFTR (Zhejiang University, CVPR 2021): detector-free matching of two photos of one scene with transformers; semi-dense matches as keypoint pairs (the form COLMAP takes). Outdoor (MegaDepth) and indoor (ScanNet) weights. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

### Limitations

- LoFTR Indoor FP32 ONNX Runtime matched all features within 0.00014 px on seven ScanNet pairs at 768 x 1024. Whole-graph TensorRT trials lost 5.27 AUC@20 points in FP16 and 2.58 AUC@10 points in FP32 on a separate 50-pair check.
- The standalone ResNetFPN TensorRT plans took about 199 ms versus 273 ms for paired portable FP32 at 768 x 1024. The matching stages stayed in PyTorch. Each variant passed a 12-pair check that included its six worst whole-graph cases.
- Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; every match is its own keypoint pair (`pairs` is `[[0, 0], [1, 1], ...]`).
- One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the match counts differ per pair.
- Match counts depend on image content. The verified ONNX export takes a fixed input size and returns variable-length matches.
- Images are converted to grayscale and matched at `long_side` (default 840, upstream's MegaDepth test size); the coarse matching holds an (H W / 64)^2 score matrix, so memory grows with the 4th power of the side. The indoor weights were evaluated by upstream at 640 x 480 (ScanNet).

### Limitations

- The standalone B and L BF16 TensorRT engines at 768 x 1024 were compared on ten shifted photos. Minimum match precision within 2 px was 96.62% for B and 95.46% for L.
- For LoMa-B at 768 x 1024 BF16, export ONNX and build TensorRT in a fresh process. On the first 50 calibrated MegaDepth pairs, AUC@5 was 64.16 portable, 62.97 with the separately built plan, and 54.30 with the bundled TensorRT export.
- Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; `pairs` are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
- One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the match counts differ per pair.
- The match count depends on the image pair. The fixed 768 x 1024 LoMa-B64 TensorRT export returns variable-length matches. On ten photos paired with shifted copies, at least 96.7% of TensorRT correspondences agreed with portable within 2 pixels in both images.
- Two resizes per image as upstream: the detector sees a long side of `long_side` (aspect kept), the descriptor a `size` x `size` square whatever the aspect ratio.
- LoMa-R uses rotation augmentation. The other variants are trained for upright images.

| `romav1` | MegaDepth-1500, every 10th pair, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees | 67.6 / 80.1 / 88.2 | 66.4 / 79.5 / 88.1 | 68.2 / 80.8 / 88.8 | 66.5 / 79.7 / 88.0 | 67.5 / 80.0 / 88.2 |  |

Measured on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks f218aa9d, 2026-11-13.

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 4.3e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.00079 and p99 <= 0.0042 (absolute error of the output `warp`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `romav1` | 0.00052 / 0.00269 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `fastbb@7d058322634d:sm_120`, `romav2@8e53c9cfd7d0:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- The fixed FP32 DINOv2 TensorRT stage raised AUC@5 from 61.60 to 64.93 on 300 MegaDepth pairs. On one pair the pose error went from 13.67 degrees to the 90-degree failure value, even with TF32 disabled.
- A separate FP32 TensorRT stage for the fine VGG encoder also introduced a pose failure on a MegaDepth pair solved by portable, with TF32 disabled.
- Restricting the FP32 engine to the fine VGG stride-8 convolutions introduced zero new pose failures on 300 MegaDepth pairs. AUC@5/10/20 changed from 63.97/77.89/87.40 to 64.00/77.92/87.29, and one pair's pose error rose from 2.58 to 22.71 degrees.
- One direction (the first image's half of upstream's symmetric call); upstream's sampling / keypoint helpers are not included; tools/eval_matching.py has the MegaDepth-1500 sampling.
- Both images are resized to squares (upstream's behaviour), whatever their aspect ratio; upstream resizes PIL images, this runner float tensors (bicubic, antialiased).

</details>

## RoMa v2

RoMa v2 (2025): dense matching between two photos of one scene from any viewpoints: where each pixel of the first image is in the second, and how sure the model is that it is visible there. Built on Meta's DINOv3. MIT code; the DINOv3 parts of the code and weights are under the DINOv3 licence.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `romav2` | synthetic (768x1024) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 1412<br>741<br>550<br>350<br>723<br>353 | 11159 / 11606<br>9881 / 10124<br>1989 / 2476<br>1890 / 2460<br>3030 / 3144<br>6694 / 6740 |

- Original code: <https://github.com/Parskatt/romav2> at `95c9968145c8`
- Code licence: MIT AND LicenseRef-DINOv3-License (permissive); files: `LICENSE`, `LICENSE.md`
- Weights licence: MIT AND LicenseRef-DINOv3-License
- Licence evidence: <https://github.com/Parskatt/romav2/blob/95c9968145c8906b7b59383258e9f73b02853d89/README.md#license>
- Training data: Upstream README: a mix of wide-baseline matching datasets following UFM and MapAnything (MegaDepth and others; see the paper); none has a dataset entry here yet. The frozen DINOv3 descriptor was pretrained on LVD-1689M (not released).
- Licence note: The checkpoint includes the DINOv3 ViT-L/16 weights, and net/dinov3.py and net/vit/ come from DINOv3: the DINOv3 License (Meta: attribution and conditions apply) covers those parts; read it before commercial use.
- Options: `coarse_size` = 800 (>= 16), `fine_size` = 1280 (>= 0), `keep_descriptors` = 0 (>= 0; speed only)

- Variants: `romav2`
- Outputs: warp, certainty

- Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): `romav2` 3000x4000 (2.9 GiB peak allocated, 4.7 reserved)
- `romav2` 768x1024, first call: portable + torch.compile 360 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 185 s (ONNX + engine).
- `romav2` original (fp32) 768x1024: upstream RoMaV2.match; local correlation: upstream's plain-torch path (no fused-local-corr)
- `romav2` original 768x1024: the authors' mixed-precision option (bfloat16); upstream RoMaV2.match; local correlation: upstream's plain-torch path (no fused-local-corr)
- `romav2` load / first call: original 5.45 s / 2.091 s, portable 0.85 s / 0.913 s, kernels 0.96 s / 0.62 s
- Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

### Measured

Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. The same 300 pairs for all modes, so float32 and bfloat16 compare pair for pair. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### Limitations

- On Apple MPS, use float32. On the RoMa reference pair, FP16 autocast in the upstream mixed-precision regions produced non-finite warp and certainty. BF16 there exceeded the warp-error tolerance on the M1 Pro.

## XFeat

XFeat (Verlab, CVPR 2024): fast sparse keypoints and descriptors, matched by mutual nearest neighbours or LighterGlue; output as keypoints plus index pairs (the form COLMAP takes). Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| `xfeat-lighterglue` | synthetic (768x1024) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 23.6<br>31.8<br>32.8<br>16.2<br>public API unavailable | 448 / 478<br>444 / 476<br>445 / 478<br>262 / 278<br>– |

- `xfeat` 768x1024, first call: portable + torch.compile 31 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp32 12 s (ONNX + engine).
- `xfeat-lighterglue` 768x1024, first call: portable + torch.compile 40 s (cold Inductor cache).
- `xfeat` original 768x1024: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; upstream XFeat.detectAndCompute + mnn, top_k 4096
- `xfeat` portable 768x1024, kernels 768x1024: Convolution and BatchNorm run separately to preserve the reference pose accuracy.
- `xfeat-lighterglue` original 768x1024: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; upstream XFeat.detectAndCompute + lighterglue, top_k 4096

- Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

### Measured

Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. Both modes receive pairs resized to 768 x 1024. Map matched pixels to the calibrated evaluation coordinates and use the same RANSAC seed per pair. The same 300 pairs for all modes, so float32 and bfloat16 compare pair for pair. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Measured on portable: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 7b65b918f / a1d55d1286e64f01e35fbf172487755e5a8a7bc4 / ec7b1307+port/p1-match, 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-20; portable32: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 7243b9b8, 2026-11-19; kernels: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 78a59767f / 7b65b918f, 2026-11-20; tensorrt: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 7243b9b8, 2026-11-19.

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 3e-05 vs the original. GPU, float32 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0001 and p99 <= 0.001 (absolute error of the output `keypoints1`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xfeat` | 0.0 / 0.0 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.10.0+cu130 | `keypoint_nms@3cfcd62bc9a5:sm_120` |
| `xfeat-lighterglue` | 0.0 / 0.0 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.10.0+cu130 | `keypoint_nms@3cfcd62bc9a5:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; `pairs` are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
- One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the keypoint counts differ per image.
- Whole-model ONNX and TensorRT export stops at the data-dependent keypoint counts. `torch.compile` runs with graph breaks.
- `xfeat` (mutual nearest neighbours) has no learned confidence: its scores are the descriptors' cosine similarities.
- On CUDA, kernels uses IEEE FP32 convolutions. Portable follows PyTorch's cuDNN precision setting. Both modes returned identical keypoints, matches and scores on 32 checked MegaDepth pairs when they used the same convolution precision.

</details>
